newsitem.title: USA: Kevorkian's lawyer asks for trial venue change.
newsitem.headline: Kevorkian's lawyer asks for trial venue change.

text.p: Jury selection in Jack Kevorkian's fourth assisted suicide trial started on Tuesday, but not before his lawyer asked for a change of venue and permission to excuse his client from attending the proceeding.

Kevorkian, 69, was charged with four felonies including violating the state's unwritten "common law" banning physician-assisted suicide for his role in the Aug. 30, death of Loretta Peabody, who suffered from multiple sclerosis.
The retired pathologist, who has admitted attending 45 deaths since 1990, also was charged with practicing medicine without a license.

At a special hearing prior to jury selection at a local movie theatre, attorney Geoffrey Fieger told Ionia County Circuit Judge Charles Miel Kevorkian would likely become impatient with the proceedings and could disrupt them.

"It was difficult for him to sit through another trial, and that gave potential for disturbance," Fieger said. He also asked the judge to change the venue, arguing that Kevorkian could not get a fair trial in the conservative, west-central Michigan town of 7,000 because of excessive publicity.

Fieger also objected to Ionia County prosecutor Ray Voet's decision to hire Michael Modelski, a former Detroit-area prosecutor with involvment in past Kevorkian cases, to assist in the case. Fieger said he intended to call Modelski as a witness, adding: "Dr. Kevorkian's rights are denied if Modelski sits here and prosecutes the case."

Miel said he would take the motions under advisement and ordered questioning of potential jurors to begin. Legal experts say Voet may have the best chance of convicting Kevorkian of any prosecutor in recent years.
Kevorkian was acquitted on assisted suicide charges once in 1994 and twice in 1996.
